verdicts.summary: Which threads get cleaned depends on whichever release removes the entry first. If the idle fiber removes it while a detach is still in progress, the detached thread is in neither `attachedThreadIds` nor `detachedThreadId`. Its roster is never cleared and the thread stays Waiting (#15239).
verdicts.scenario: 1) An exclusive Claude session S has one thread T. T's projection roster lists [dev-server], but the adapter's in-memory roster is empty, so idle release is allowed. 2) The user archives T. `detach` runs `Ref.modify` (2487-2503) and stores `updatedEntry`, whose `attachedThreadIds` no longer contains T. `idleGeneration` is unchanged because it is spread from `entry`. 3) Before `releaseEntry` runs at 2528, while `cancelIdleFiber` and `clearMcpSession` are yielding, the session idle fiber fires. It calls `releaseEntry(onlyIfIdleGeneration)`. `removeLiveEntry` (976-1000) takes `updatedEntry` as the candidate and removes it, because `busyTurns` is 0 and the generation matches. 4) `readReleasedBackgroundTasks` gets no `detachedThreadId` and an empty `attachedThreadIds`, so it reads no threads and returns []. 5) The detach's own `releaseEntry` then finds no entry (980) and does nothing. T's roster stays, so T shows Waiting until restart. The window is narrow (milliseconds) and needs the idle timer to fire during an archive.
verdicts.consequence: The thread keeps showing Waiting after archive or detach, which is the exact bug this change fixes, until a server restart.

verdicts.summary: The release write is a `provider-thread.updated` event for the released provider thread. Applying it always sets `thread.activeProviderThreadId` to that thread. After a Claude→Codex switch, the detach effect runs after the new provider thread became active, so the thread points back at the dead Claude provider thread.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Thread T ran on Claude: provider thread P1, session S1, roster [dev-server]. 2) The user switches T to Codex and sends a message. For `create_with_handoff`, `ProviderSwitchService` puts S1 in `releaseProviderSessionIds` (ProviderSwitchService.ts:194-195). 3) The queued-run command commits `provider-thread.updated` for the new P2 (Orchestrator.ts:1878-1884), so active = P2. It also enqueues the effects [provider-session.detach S1, provider-turn.start] (1905-1920). 4) The outbox runs one effect per thread at a time, in order (EffectOutbox.ts:329-361), so the detach runs first. `releaseEntry` → `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` writes P1 with an empty roster and `updatedAt=now`. ProjectionStore.ts:2264 sets `activeProviderThreadId=P1` and bumps the thread's `updatedAt`. 5) Until ProviderTurnStartService.ts:873 writes P2 again, the active thread is P1. In that window the shell goal comes from P1 (ProjectionStore.ts:1534-1537), feedback upload targets P1 (ws.ts:2281-2285), and checkpoint rollback targets P1 and S1 (Orchestrator.ts:9672). Before this change no release wrote a provider-thread row, so this did not happen. I did not verify whether every turn-start failure path before line 873 rewrites P2. If one does not, the flip persists.
verdicts.consequence: The thread briefly points at the old Claude provider thread: wrong goal shown, feedback and rollback aimed at a dead session. This could persist if the Codex start fails before the running write.
verdicts.missing: Whether ProviderTurnStartService/RunExecutionService failure paths before ProviderTurnStartService.ts:873 rewrite P2 when the Codex session open fails.
